newsitem.title: SHARJAH: CRICKET-DE SILVA REACHES 6,000 RUNS LANDMARK IN CUP WIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-DE SILVA REACHES 6,000 RUNS LANDMARK IN CUP WIN.

text.p: Aravinda de Silva became the first Sri Lankan to score 6,000 runs in one-day internationals as his team swept to victory in the opening match of the Sharjah Cup on Thursday.
De Silva reached the landmark during his innings of 60 that helped the World Cup champions to beat Zimbabwe by seven wickets with 4.2 overs to spare.
Zimbabwe were restricted to 187 for nine in their 50 overs, paceman Chaminda Vaas taking three for 25 in his 10 overs, and Sri Lanka romped home at 188 for three in 45.4 overs.

Flamboyant opener Sanath Jayasuriya, named this week as one of Wisden's five cricketers of the year, led the Sri Lankan charge with a fluent 56 of 74 balls, lashing seven fours, and one six off pace bowler Eddo Brandes.
Unruffled by the loss of opening partner Romesh Kaluwitharana for a duck, Jayasuriya repaired the damage in a second-wicket stand of 79 with Marvan Atapattu, who hit 52 not out.
De Silva and Atapattu then put on 107 for the third wicket to clinch victory.
Man-of-the-match de Silva, playing his 199th limited overs international, is the ninth player in the world to reach the 6,000 runs milestone.
